correctness.rationale: For each fixed labeled fine-degree tuple, every input homogeneous component is zero- or one-dimensional, so the multilinear quotient has dimension at most one. If two or more nonzero basis degrees occur with odd multiplicity, the total degree lies outside the support and the component is zero. If at most one occurs oddly, pairing equal-degree variables first gives a nonzero evaluation because each orthogonal basis vector has nonzero square. Thus the per-tuple dimension is exactly the stated parity indicator. Fourier inversion on \((\mathbb Z/2)^n\) then gives the closed character sum and hence the binomial formula; the unique leading absolute base \(n+1\) gives the growth exponent. The bundled finite checker agrees with the symbolic count and is used only as a consistency check.

originality.rationale: The decisive primary source already gives essentially the same parity basis. Proposition 3.24 states, for infinite fields, that the quotient basis is the set from Lemma 3.22; Lemma 3.25 and Theorem 3.26 give the finite-field basis, whose monomials have all degree multiplicities even except possibly one. In the multilinear component each variable occurs once, so the finite-field exponent cap is irrelevant, and the published basis immediately makes each labeled degree component zero or one with exactly the submitted parity criterion. Summing those components by elementary character orthogonality yields the displayed codimension formula. Under the implication standard, this is a routine enumerative corollary of the published basis, not an original theorem merely because the word 'codimension' is absent.
